verdict.text: The login step now fails at the OIDC read when GitHub's response has no usable `value`, before it masks anything or calls Vault.
The new test checks every clause of row r1's `fails_when`, and the gates are green.
Pass.
Read the diff of `.github/actions/lab-auth/action.yml` and the full login step.
`jq -er '.value // empty'` exits nonzero when there is no output.
Under `set -euo pipefail`, that failure, or a curl failure, reaches the `|| { ::error::...; exit 1; }` branch.
This is the same pattern the step already uses for the Vault token.
Ran the step's script directly with a stub curl, both the fixed version and the old `jq -r .value` version.
With `{}` or `{"value":null}`, the fixed script exits 1 with the `::error::` line, and no mask or Vault call happens.
The old script prints `::add-mask::null`, calls Vault and exits 0.
With `{"value":"abc"}`, both versions mask `abc` and log in, so the happy path is unchanged.
Row r1: `test_login_fails_on_missing_oidc_value` runs the real step text read from action.yml under `bash -e -o pipefail`.
It stubs only curl, which is the network boundary.
It asserts a nonzero exit, no Vault call (marker file), no `::add-mask::null`, and an `::error::` line naming the OIDC token.
Each assertion fails against the old line.
Row r2 and the gates: `loopctl gate stamp` returned pass for pre_commit, cli_tests, eval-row r1 and eval-row r2.
Stamp green bc6b7f8426c55786141380ab6d2e3c058d098580d6dd2b22bbdb831f4f0f07c0.
Consistency: grep found no doc or `.okf` page that quotes the old `jq -r .value` line.
None.
The `::error::` message also fires when curl itself fails, for example on an HTTP error from the token endpoint.
curl's own `-sS` stderr line still prints above it, so the cause stays visible.
